newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares pare gains but still close higher.
newsitem.headline: German shares pare gains but still close higher.

text.p: Profit-taking chipped away at German share market gains in calm floor trading on Wednesday but the blue-chip DAX index still closed the session with gains, underpinned by several shares' strong performances.
Wall Street's strong gains on Tuesday, a stable dollar, as well as demand for chemical group shares and car makers Volkswagen AG and Daimler AG contributed to the day's gains.
The 30-share DAX index closed trading up 4.32 points at 2,563.16, after having traded in a range between 2,571.69 and 2,563.01.

Dealers had expected range-bound trading for the floor session and also forecast the same for the afternoon session, saying the market needed something more significant to ferry it back towards the 2,600 level.
Biggest trading volumes in early bourse trade were in chemical companies, with foreign investors seeking to line their portfolios with German chemical stocks.

But at the end of the session Hoechst AG was the only one of the three big chemical groups to hold onto gains, closing up 86 pfennigs at 53.01. Meanwhile profit-taking sent BASF AG shares down 11 pfennigs to 44.28 and Bayer AG shares down 16 pfennigs to 53.85.
Carmaker Volkswagen ended up nearly three percent at 551.50 marks after it said its car deliveries in western Europe were up 11.3 percent to 1.451 million vehicles.
There was strong interest in industrial giant Daimler Benz early on, which was up 1.37 marks at 81.32 marks at the end of the session in advance of half-year figures, due Thursday.
